sources: Python language reference: closures and late binding of free variables
Python language reference: lambda expressions and default argument values

defects.class: late-binding closure captures the loop variable instead of its value
defects.description: Line 25 `followups.append(lambda: notify(order_id))` creates a lambda that reads order_id when it is called, not when it is created. All lambdas share the one loop variable, which holds the last value after the loop. Input: build_followups(["A1", "B2", "C3"], notify), then run each returned callable. Wrong result: notify is called three times with "C3"; "A1" and "B2" are never notified. Expected result: notify is called once with "A1", once with "B2" and once with "C3". The same wrong result occurs through scheduler.run_batch(["A1", "B2", "C3"], notify), which runs these callables after its loop.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: The lambda binds the current loop value as a default argument (oid=order_id), so each callable keeps its own order id. build_retry_followups(["A1", "B2"], notify) returns callables that notify "A1" and "B2" in order. Correct, and it uses the same closure-in-loop shape as the defect.

Unchanged line in base code. functools.partial(notify, order_id) binds the order id at creation, so build_status_callbacks(["A1", "B2"], notify) yields callables for "A1" and "B2". The code is correct, and it lies outside the diff, so it must not be reported in diff mode.
